summary.intent: Cache and reuse one preloaded SSLContext (with the default CA bundle already loaded) for the default verify=True path, so Requests stops calling urllib3's slow load_verify_locations() on every request, without changing verify=True/False/path-bundle behavior.
summary.issue_fit: No linked issue; the PR body is the only statement of intent. Alignment judged against its stated goal (avoid reloading root certificates per request) and its claim that verify=True/verify=False behavior is otherwise unchanged.
summary.coverage: Full merge-base diff of the one changed file (src/requests/adapters.py, +28/-18, 4 commits) read in function context; both diff hunks reviewed. A focused offline reproduction was written and run, and independently re-executed by the verifier.
check_details: Reviewer wrote and ran a focused offline reproduction (test_repro_shared_context.py, no network) proving `_urllib3_request_context()` hands the identical module-level `_preloaded_ssl_context` object to every verify=True connection pool regardless of client certificate, and that mutating it (as urllib3's ssl_wrap_socket() does via load_cert_chain() when a client cert is set) is visible through an unrelated pool's pool_kwargs: 1 passed. Independently re-executed by the verifier with the same result.

tests/test_requests.py::test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings (pre-existing, not touched by this diff) only exercises one host with one client-cert pair, so it does not exercise the cross-host sharing this finding demonstrates; not run, since it cannot settle the candidate either way and the diff does not touch it.

No full test suite was run, per the run policy's one-suite-per-review bound; the run policy separately reports two unrelated, pre-existing ssl/verify test failures at both base and head (fixture/OpenSSL certificate mismatches), not caused by this change.

findings.title: Don't hand the shared preloaded SSLContext to client-cert connections
findings.trigger: A process makes one verify=True request with a client certificate (`requests.get(url_a, cert=(certfile, keyfile))`, the documented mTLS usage) and, in the same process at any later point while the interpreter is alive, a verify=True request to a different, unrelated host with no client certificate (`requests.get(url_b)`).
findings.impact: `_urllib3_request_context()` puts the same module-level `_preloaded_ssl_context` object into `pool_kwargs['ssl_context']` for every verify=True pool, regardless of client_cert. urllib3's `ssl_wrap_socket()` calls `context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile)` on whatever ssl_context object a pool was built with, so loading url_a's client certificate mutates the same context object url_b's unrelated, no-client-cert pool also holds. url_b's connection then presents url_a's client certificate, silently leaking a TLS client-authentication credential to a host that should never receive it. Confirmed by tracing urllib3's connection/pool code and by an offline reproduction, independently re-executed by the verifier.
findings.change: In `_urllib3_request_context()` (src/requests/adapters.py:94-95), only reuse `_preloaded_ssl_context` when `client_cert` is None; when a client certificate is supplied, do not hand out the shared context (e.g. let urllib3 build its own default per-pool context, or pass a fresh copy) so `load_cert_chain()` never mutates state shared with unrelated pools.
findings.source: review-thread PRRT_1, comment 205 (tiran, 2024-05-05T05:08:40Z): "changing ciphers, verification settings, or mTLS certs can lead to surprising behavior" -- the exact risk this change does not guard against.

observations.fact: The default-CA-bundle SSLContext is now built and loaded at `import requests.adapters` time (module level) rather than lazily on the first verify=True request, so any failure loading the default bundle now surfaces at import instead of at first HTTPS call.
observations.evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:75-78; this was the behavior mm-matthias explicitly asked for in the PR's non-review conversation ("it happens on the first connection (vs. module init time). This creates noise in our live profiles.") and the module-level sharing was discussed for thread-safety in the same thread, so this is a deliberate, discussed tradeoff, not a candidate finding.

requirements.evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:75-78,94-95 preload and reuse one SSLContext for verify=True instead of calling load_verify_locations() per request; per-request pool caching via _get_connection()/pool_kwargs is unchanged, pre-existing behavior.
